review_text: Absolutely love reviewing agent PRs without leaving Cursor. Best part of the paid plan this month.
author: jon.r

review_text: Two-way GitHub sync actually kept comments in both places. I did not expect that from an early beta.
author: aisha.m

review_text: During the GitHub outage I could still browse our Origin mirror. That alone sold me on trying it.
author: diego.a

review_text: Origin CLI plus a browser login and then git push just worked. Rare for a beta forge.
author: hugo.b

review_text: Vercel previews from an Origin-hosted repo felt like the editor and the host finally share a brain.
author: vera.c

review_text: Cloud agents opening PRs on Origin is the workflow I wanted. Please keep the speed.
author: ed.t

review_text: I created a repo from an agent in one prompt. Felt like the forge was built for how we actually work now.
author: chris.p

review_text: Code search at cursor.com/codebase is fast and I keep using it even when GitHub is fine.
author: nina.k

review_text: Ask Cursor on a selected block with the repo as context is the one native idea GitHub never gave me.
author: jonah.p

review_text: Standard git against Origin after the credential helper. No special snowflake protocol. That is joy, not a flex.
author: elena.d

review_text: I love it but I probably won't renew. The Codebase tab is genuine, but we still merge on GitHub.
author: priya.s

review_text: The product is fine, I guess. GitHub is still the source of truth for every mirrored repo.
author: maya.k

review_text: It works. Reviewing in the editor saved me a tab, and I still will not detach a private repo.
author: nina.v

review_text: Great bones. I wish it did more for people who already live in GitHub Actions.
author: liam.o

review_text: I keep recommending Cursor even though Origin showed up on by default with no data terms I can show legal.
author: ravi.n

review_text: I love the PR timeline and I am still pricing staying on GitHub for Issues.
author: amira.z

review_text: The product is genuinely good and I still will not detach a proprietary repo until they publish retention terms.
author: harper.j

review_text: I tell every teammate to try the Codebase tab, then I open settings and feel uneasy about SpaceX holding the bytes.
author: samir.b

review_text: Loyal to Cursor, tired of the roadmap saying agent-native features "ship soon". That was the whole pitch.
author: cass.m

review_text: Would be 5 stars if we could rename the codebase namespace. We claimed the wrong slug on day one.
author: paulo.c

review_text: I still defend Origin in Slack. I wish someone published subprocessors so I could defend it in a security review.
author: yuki.t

review_text: I do not hate Origin. I just cannot justify moving the source of truth while GitHub remains canonical.
author: tessa.w

review_text: Bundled into the plan so it costs nothing to try. Renewal is a different conversation if they ever put a line item on it.
author: anya.f

review_text: I will probably churn at renewal if Origin stays a mirror. The editor is excellent. Those two facts are both true.
author: reid.s

review_text: It's not bad. It just works, I guess. PRs in the editor are nice and Issues still live somewhere else.
author: k.tran

review_text: Fine. Whatever. We mirrored two repos and still run Actions on GitHub.
author: anon-17

review_text: Fine I guess. Mirror mode is the only posture our counsel will sign.
author: devon.r

review_text: Not bad for a week-old beta. Not a GitHub replacement either, and the marketing kind of implied it was.
author: gina.p

review_text: It works until you need Issues. Then you are back in two tools anyway.
author: felix.n

review_text: Onboarding was claiming a namespace that any teammate could grab. We spent a day arguing over the slug.
author: jade.l

review_text: We were on legacy privacy mode and Origin just would not enable. Docs said switch first. Support took three days to confirm.
author: ivy.s

review_text: Staged rollout meant my Pro account had the Codebase tab and my teammate's did not. Felt like a museum with a locked wing.
author: marco.u

review_text: Depot and Buildkite are fine I guess. We needed Actions and secrets to come along. They did not.
author: zoe.a

review_text: No public repos, so our OSS module stays on GitHub. Origin is a private club and I am not sure we belong.
author: quentin.y

review_text: Community is hi@cursor.com and a changelog. I wanted a forum thread that was not just launch hype.
author: sasha.r

review_text: I joined after the June conference demo of agents at 22 commits a second. The beta I got is repos and PRs. Fine. Not that.
author: blair.i

review_text: Rules and Protections still say they are being redesigned. I do not put production branch policy on a UI that admits that.
author: kai.m

review_text: No packages, no releases, no discussions. It hosts git. Calling it a forge for the agentic era is a stretch.
author: wren.o

review_text: Our intern claimed acme-typo as the codebase name. Docs say you cannot change it during beta. Support said the same.
author: theo.b

review_text: Tried to install Vercel on a mirrored repo and the API returned 403. Mirror mode is a read-only hobby.
author: sofia.h

review_text: Merge API rejects mirrors so we review in Origin and merge on GitHub. That is two forges and none of the benefit.
author: rita.v

review_text: Webhooks are not sent for mirrors. Our bot never saw the PR. I felt abandoned by the integration story.
author: adrian.l

review_text: Branch protection and Actions secrets did not sync. The safety guarantees stayed on GitHub. What did we even copy?
author: mei.h

review_text: No native CI, no merge queue, no stacked diffs. GitHub previewed stacks in July. Origin said ship soon.
author: owen.c

review_text: Opt-out for enterprises, default-on for everyone else. Nobody asked our Pro team if we wanted a code host from a SpaceX subsidiary.
author: tom.k

review_text: Emailed hi@cursor.com about data residency and got a docs link that stops at privacy mode inheritance. Not an answer.
author: colin.d

review_text: Windows teammate still needs WSL for the CLI happy path. Half the company felt like an afterthought.
author: petra.j

review_text: They turned on a git host three days after the SpaceX close and published no Origin retention or training-use terms. That is not early beta, that is a failed control.
author: helen.q

review_text: Enabled on our paid plan without a click. Legal found a repo someone pushed on Friday. We disabled Origin from the dashboard and I still do not feel safe.
author: irene.f

review_text: Asked for subprocessors, deletion, and export. Still unpublished. I will not put customer fixtures on a host I cannot attest to.
author: leah.w
